title: Can AI pick stocks? AI investing apps to try
summary: AI can pick stocks that fit your portfolio, but it can’t guarantee winners. We compare five AI investing apps, including our own.
body_markdown:
## Which AI investing apps should you try?


We cover four apps first, in our order, and finish with our top pick.


### Magnifi


**What it is.** An AI investing app from Magnifi LLC, an SEC-registered investment adviser. You can ask its assistant about your holdings, research new ideas, backtest strategies and screen stocks, ETFs and mutual funds in plain English. It links taxable brokerage accounts, IRAs, 401(k)s and 529 plans through Plaid, read-only, and can review the fees you pay on your funds.


**Price.** A free plan, and Premium at $14 a month or $99 a year.


**Best for.** Investors who hold a lot of funds and want to understand fees and overlap, on iPhone, Android or the web.


**Limits.** Trades happen only in a Magnifi Investment Account at an unaffiliated broker such as Apex Clearing or E*Trade, and your other linked accounts are view-only.


### Danelfin


**What it is.** A stock-scoring tool. Every day it gives US stocks, US-listed ETFs and major European stocks an AI Score from 1 to 10. Danelfin says the score estimates how likely a stock is to do better than its benchmark over the next three months, using technical, fundamental and sentiment indicators.


**Price.** Free, then Plus at $29 a month, Pro at $79 and Elite at $179, with lower annual prices.


**Best for.** Investors with a watchlist who want a consistent way to decide what to research first, on the web, iPhone or Android.


**Limits.** Danelfin says its scores aren’t personalized investment advice and calculate probabilities, not certainties. A high score can’t tell you whether the stock adds to a sector you already hold too much of.


### AInvest


**What it is.** An AI research platform built around Aime, an assistant that can run multi-step research, build screeners, backtest ideas and set up automations from one prompt.


**Price.** A free Basic plan. Paid plans run from Pro at $59.99 a month to Terminal at $999.99 a month, with yearly discounts.


**Best for.** Hands-on investors who want a research assistant that can build screens and tests quickly, on the web, iPhone, Android, Mac or Windows.


**Limits.** AInvest says it isn’t a broker-dealer or registered investment adviser. Its terms say Aime doesn’t consider your individual investment objectives and that a research answer doesn’t place a trade.


### TrendSpider


**What it is.** A charting and technical analysis platform for active traders. It automates chart analysis, runs scanners across the market, backtests strategies and lets you train machine-learning models on trading signals. Its assistant, Sidekick, can review charts, read filings and set up scans and alerts. Trading bots follow the entry and exit rules you configure, through more than 30 connected brokers and crypto exchanges.


**Price.** Four paid plans, from Standard to Advanced, with a paid trial. Prices were discounted for a sale in November 2026, so check its pricing page.


**Best for.** Traders who make decisions on price action and want to test rules before risking money.


**Limits.** TrendSpider’s terms say it doesn’t provide investment advice. It’s built for charts and short-term signals, so it does less for a long-term investor reviewing a portfolio.


### Our top pick: Astor


**What it is.** A[personal investing agent](https://www.astor.app/blog/what-is-a-personal-investing-agent) . It connects to your brokerage, retirement and crypto accounts at most major US institutions, such as Robinhood, Schwab and Coinbase. It follows every position you own and texts you over iMessage or WhatsApp when something matters to your portfolio.


**How it recommends trades.** After a short risk assessment, you and Astor agree on a target mix for your money. Astor then recommends specific buys and sells with dollar amounts, based on that target, everything you hold, your risk level, taxes and preferences. When you ask for new ideas, it leaves out what you already own and says why each name made the list. With[Text to Trade](https://www.astor.app/blog/introducing-text-to-trade) , available on Max plans, you approve each order and it executes in your own Robinhood agentic account.


**Price.** Free to start with no card. Pro is $19 a month or $10 a month billed yearly, and Max is $29 a month or $19 a month billed yearly.


**Best for.** People who already invest and want new ideas judged against what they own.


**Limits.** The app is iPhone only, with no Android or web app, though people on Android can text Astor on WhatsApp. It’s US only and doesn’t run a managed portfolio. The AI can be wrong, which is why it shows its sources and you make the call.
